functions.name: MatrixBase::applyOnTheLeft
functions.signature:
template <typename Derived>
void Eigen::MatrixBase<Derived>::applyOnTheLeft(Eigen::Index p, Eigen::Index q, const Eigen::JacobiRotation<typename Derived::Scalar>& j);
functions.description: Applies the given Jacobi (Givens) plane rotation to this matrix on the left, i.e., it rotates rows p and q in-place. This is typically used in algorithms such as QR, SVD, or diagonalization to zero out elements by mixing two rows using the rotation j. Call on a non-const matrix/expression to update it directly.
requirements: This must be called on a mutable (non-const) Eigen::MatrixBase object; it modifies the matrix in-place.
Indices p and q must be valid row indices for the current matrix: 0 <= p < rows() and 0 <= q < rows().
The rotation must be compatible with the matrix scalar type: j is an Eigen::JacobiRotation<typename Derived::Scalar>.
Behavior for p == q is unspecified by this header; callers should provide two (typically distinct) valid row indices.
Matrix/expression must be in a state that allows row access and modification (i.e., not an rvalue temporary).

functions.name: MatrixBase::applyOnTheRight
functions.signature:
template <typename Derived>
void Eigen::MatrixBase<Derived>::applyOnTheRight(Eigen::Index p, Eigen::Index q, const Eigen::JacobiRotation<typename Derived::Scalar>& j);
functions.description: Applies the given Jacobi (Givens) plane rotation to this matrix on the right, i.e., it rotates columns p and q in-place. This is commonly used to affect column pairs in algorithms like QR, SVD, or Hessenberg/Schur transformations using the rotation j. Call on a non-const matrix/expression to update it directly.
requirements: This must be called on a mutable (non-const) Eigen::MatrixBase object; it modifies the matrix in-place.
Indices p and q must be valid column indices for the current matrix: 0 <= p < cols() and 0 <= q < cols().
The rotation must be compatible with the matrix scalar type: j is an Eigen::JacobiRotation<typename Derived::Scalar>.
Behavior for p == q is unspecified by this header; callers should provide two (typically distinct) valid column indices.
Matrix/expression must be in a state that allows column access and modification (i.e., not an rvalue temporary).

functions.name: Eigen::MatrixBase::eigenvalues
functions.description: Computes and returns the eigenvalues of a matrix expression. Intended for square matrices and returns a (complex) column vector of eigenvalues using Eigen’s generic eigenvalue solver. Use this as a convenience method when you only need eigenvalues; for more control or to also obtain eigenvectors, use Eigen::EigenSolver or specialized solvers. Note: The exact concrete return type is an Eigen-defined helper alias (EigenvaluesReturnType<Derived>) which evaluates to a complex-valued vector of size rows().
requirements: The input matrix expression must be square (rows() == cols()); otherwise this is ill-formed or triggers an assertion (requirement inferred from function semantics and Eigen naming).
The matrix object/expression must be a valid, initialized Eigen matrix or matrix expression (i.e., no dangling references).
Numeric values should be finite for meaningful results; behavior with NaN/Inf is unspecified (inferred).
Include the Eigenvalues module (e.g., #include <Eigen/Eigenvalues>) so this extension is available.

functions.name: Eigen::MatrixBase::operatorNorm
functions.signature:
template <typename Derived>
typename Eigen::NumTraits<typename Derived::Scalar>::Real Eigen::MatrixBase<Derived>::operatorNorm() const;
functions.description: Computes the operator 2-norm (spectral norm) of a matrix expression, i.e., the largest singular value. Returns a non-negative real scalar regardless of the matrix’s scalar type (real part for complex types). This is a convenience method implemented via Eigen’s eigenvalue/singular-value routines and is suitable when only the norm is needed.
requirements: The matrix/expression must be a valid, initialized Eigen matrix or matrix expression.
Numeric values should be finite for meaningful results; behavior with NaN/Inf is unspecified (inferred).
Include the Eigenvalues module (e.g., #include <Eigen/Eigenvalues>) so this extension is available.

functions.name: qMalloc
functions.description: Allocates a block of heap memory using Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc with Eigen’s alignment guarantees (suitable for vectorized operations). Intended as a Qt-style replacement for malloc that returns an aligned pointer.
requirements: size must specify the number of bytes to allocate; behavior for size == 0 is unknown (not documented here).
The returned pointer must be released with qFree (or a function compatible with Eigen::internal::aligned_free).

The allocation has no explicit error handling; if allocation fails and a null pointer is returned by Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc, callers must detect and handle a null return before dereferencing.

functions.name: qFree
functions.description: Frees a memory block previously allocated by qMalloc (or Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc) using Eigen::internal::aligned_free. Intended as a Qt-style replacement for free that matches qMalloc’s allocation.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by qMalloc (or Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc) and not already freed.
ptr must not be used after this call (no use-after-free).
Behavior for ptr == nullptr is unknown based on this header; consult Eigen::internal::aligned_free or pass non-null to be safe.

functions.name: qRealloc
functions.description: Reallocates an aligned memory block by allocating a new block with Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc(size), copying exactly size bytes with std::memcpy, freeing the old block with Eigen::internal::aligned_free, and returning the new pointer. Unlike standard realloc, this implementation unconditionally copies size bytes and provides no failure handling.
requirements: ptr must point to a valid, allocated memory block (from qMalloc or Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc) that is readable for at least size bytes; otherwise std::memcpy will overread.
size must be less than or equal to the number of bytes originally allocated for ptr to avoid reading beyond the old allocation during memcpy.
If size is smaller than the original allocation, only the first size bytes are preserved; the remainder is discarded.

This function does not check for allocation failure; if Eigen::internal::aligned_malloc(size) returns nullptr, the subsequent std::memcpy will dereference a null pointer and crash. Callers must ensure sufficient memory is available or wrap this in higher-level checks.
ptr must not be nullptr (null) because std::memcpy would read from a null source; behavior would be undefined.
The old pointer (ptr) must not be used after this call; it is freed unconditionally.
